name: Shadowy Men On A Shadowy Planet

info.bio: Shadowy Men on a Shadowy Planet was a Canadian instrumental rock band with a strong surf influence, formed in 1984. The band members were: Don Pyle on drums, Brian Connelly on guitar, and Reid Diamond on bass, who died in 2001. They released a string of EPs and singles throughout the 1980s and early 1990s, achieving some success, but remain best-known for the track “Having an Average Weekend”, which was used as the theme song to the TV show The Kids in the Hall.

scenes.name: Roots-rock de los ochenta y cow-punk
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Como en 1970 tras 1966, la new wave de 1976 va seguida de un revival del roots-rock, esta vez gradual y disfrazado: punks que desfiguran los estilos tradicionales (X, Dream Syndicate, Gun Club) y los «cow-punks» que tocan country ambientado entre inadaptados: Long Ryders, Jason & The Scorchers, Fetchin Bones, Lone Justice, Beat Farmers. El populismo de Los Lobos, Del Fuegos, Del-Lords y Walkabouts; en la Costa Oeste, los dementes Camper Van Beethoven, Donner Party, Catheads, Thin White Rope y los American Music Club de Mark Eitzel; en Texas, Wild Seeds, Poi Dog Pondering, Glass Eye; en los Grandes Lagos, BoDeans, Soul Asylum, Afghan Whigs, Shrimp Boat y los canadienses Cowboy Junkies. Nashville se renueva con los neotradicionalistas (George Strait, Randy Travis, Garth Brooks, Lyle Lovett, Steve Earle, Dwight Yoakam) y el surf instrumental vuelve con Shadowy Men On A Shadowy Planet.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breakup and Subsequent Reunion (2012)
podcast.body: The band initially broke up, leading members to join various other indie bands. However, they reunited in 2012 in a reunion that "seemed to have stuck," resulting in occasional gigs, a box set, and re-releases of their older material. "The band broke up and then everybody bounced through a long series of indie bands. [...] It much happened until 2012 when there was a reunion that seemed to have stuck."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Band Origins and Punk Roots
podcast.body: The band was formed by two musicians from Calgary who relocated to Toronto, where they initially participated in a series of "doomed punk bands" before eventually collaborating to form Shadowy Men on a Shadowy Planet. "The We Men were built around two guys from Calgary who moved to Toronto to be involved in a series of doomed punk bands before they co-listed as this band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Band's Active Periods
podcast.body: The band was active from 1984 to 1996, and then started playing occasional shows again in 2012. "It lasted from 1984 to 1996, but started playing the occasional show again in 2012."

podcast.title: Collaboration with Fred Schneider
podcast.body: Shadowy Men on a Shadowy Planet served as the backing band for Fred Schneider of The B-52s for some of his solo material, showcasing their versatility and respected musicianship. "And that time when Fred Schneider of the B-52s needed a backing band for some of his solo stuff."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: EPs and Juno Award
podcast.body: The group released a number of EPs during their active period and received a Juno Award in the category of Best Instrumental Artist, recognizing their unique instrumental sound. "There were a number of EPs, a June Award for Best Instrumental Artist."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Producer Collaboration
podcast.body: Steve Elveni, a producer/engineer known for his work with bands like Nirvana and The Pixies, was such a fan of Shadowy Men on a Shadowy Planet that he worked on one of their albums for free. "Steve Elveni, the producer slash engineer known for working with Nirvana and the pixies and so many more, liked shadowy men so much that he worked on one of their albums for free."
